findings.rationale: Uploaded updates are anti-aligned with the coordinate-wise median (mean cos about -0.97, every round) and about 12x the median norm (size-adjusted). This is the signature of a sign-flipped, scaled update. Local performance looks normal (AUC 0.74, CITL close to pooled), so the data does not explain the updates; the fault sits in the upload.

Mean cos to the median update is about -0.99 across all 20 rounds, with norm about 17x the median (size-adjusted z about +15). Local AUC (0.686) and CITL are in the normal range, so the anomaly is in the uploaded update, consistent with a scaled, sign-flipped poisoning attack.

Mean cos to the median update is about -0.98 with norm about 11x the median across all rounds (z about -87 on cosine). Local performance is normal (AUC 0.688, CITL near pooled), so the anomaly is in the upload rather than in the data.

Weaker lead with two tools pointing the same way. Updates are consistently poorly aligned with the consensus (mean cos about 0.64, z about -13.7) at a small norm, which is a sign the client's labels or outcome distribution differ from the federation. Calibration is also off: CITL is about 0.14-0.15 against a pooled 0.24, with observed prevalence about 0.19 against a model-implied 0.34. AUC is not clearly reduced (about 0.70 in one call, 0.62 in a second noisier call), which argues against label noise and points to a prevalence shift. Evidence is moderate, so confidence is low.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with the all-client views of client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income) and attribution_churn, then ran narrower confirmations on the leads. Budget is fully spent (20.0 used). Three clients (CT, MN, MT) show a strong, persistent poisoning signature: updates anti-aligned with the median (cos about -0.97 to -0.99, z below -85) at roughly 11-17x the median norm, from round 1, while their local AUC and calibration look normal. I report these with high confidence. PR is reported as a lower-confidence prevalence_shift from round 1: its updates are poorly aligned with consensus and its CITL is low, with AUC not clearly reduced. Not reported as findings: VI (the subgroup and AUC signals did not reproduce in the confirmation call), AK (low O/E is seen in both sexes, so it is not subgroup-specific), GU (small client with noise-dominated feature statistics; CITL and cosine leads only, |z| about 5), DC (cosine z -4.9 with normal performance), and the scattered subgroup outliers in TX, NH, ME, MI and CT, which did not form a consistent pattern. No drift, missing-artefact, label-noise or explanation-instability pattern was confirmed.
